cards.explanation: The answer is that he investigates everything from the beginning. The writer says it seemed good to write after "…having carefully investigated everything from the beginning…" (Luke 1:3). The homework came before the pen. I respect that, friends. I once pulled a batch without checking the oven first, and the cookies told on me. Careful beats quick every time.

The answer is certainty. The writer says the goal is "…so that you may know the certainty of the things you have been taught." (Luke 1:4). That's the whole goal: Theophilus, the man he's writing to, can know it for sure. No guessing and no fog, just solid ground under his feet, like a good batch of dough that holds its shape.

The answer is False. Luke 1:6 says Zechariah and Elizabeth were "…righteous in the sight of God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and decrees of the Lord." Both of them, together. I can't even keep a neat apron through one batch, friends, so that kind of steady walking impresses me.

The answer is that he is chosen by lot. The text says Zechariah "…was chosen by lot, according to the custom of the priesthood…" (Luke 1:9). So this was the way the priests did it. Zechariah was chosen, and he went in to burn incense.

The answer is True. Luke says that at the hour of the incense offering, "…the whole congregation was praying outside." (Luke 1:10). The whole congregation, friends, not just a few folks. While Zechariah was inside, a crowd was outside praying.

The answer is that he is startled and gripped with fear. That's how Luke tells it: "…he was startled and gripped with fear." (Luke 1:12). Honestly, I'd be right there with him. If an angel showed up next to my oven, my mustache would be standing straight up. It's a very human reaction.

The answer is True. The angel says, "Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son…" (Luke 1:13). He says it right after telling Zechariah that his prayer has been heard. Think about it, friends: this couple had no children (Luke 1:7), and this is the news that was coming.

The answer is False. The angel says John will be a joy and delight to Zechariah, and then adds, "…many will rejoice at his birth…" (Luke 1:14). So the angel doesn't stop at Zechariah's joy. He says many will rejoice.

The answer is the Holy Spirit. The angel says John "…will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother’s womb." (Luke 1:15). From his mother's womb, friends. That's before he's even born. I think that's a pretty big deal.

The answer is the disobedient. The angel says John will "…turn the hearts of the fathers to their children and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous…" (Luke 1:17). Two turnings in one sentence. The disobedient are the ones he turns to wisdom.

The answer is people. The angel says John will "…make ready a people prepared for the Lord." (Luke 1:17). People, bakers, not a building. It's about getting folks ready. That's close to my own job, helping bakers get ready for the big day.

The answer is that he and his wife are both old. Zechariah says, "I am an old man, and my wife is well along in years." (Luke 1:18). That's the reason he gives, and it matches what Luke told us earlier (Luke 1:7). I won't argue with a man about his age, friends. I don't even have one.

The answer is that he will be silent and unable to speak. Gabriel says, "…you will be silent and unable to speak…" because Zechariah did not believe his words (Luke 1:20). When Zechariah comes out, he really can't speak to the people (Luke 1:22). The people realize he has seen a vision, and he keeps making signs to them (Luke 1:22).

The answer is until the day this comes to pass. Gabriel says Zechariah will be silent and unable to speak "…until the day this comes to pass…" (Luke 1:20). The silence lasts until the promise happens. That's a long stretch of quiet for a man with news to share. I can't go five minutes without talking, friends.

The answer is True. The text says that when Zechariah came out and couldn't speak, "…they realized he had seen a vision in the temple." (Luke 1:22). They'd been waiting for him and wondering why he took so long (Luke 1:21). He also kept making signs to them (Luke 1:22).

The answer is her disgrace among the people. Elizabeth says, "In these days He has shown me favor and taken away my disgrace among the people." (Luke 1:25). She gives the credit to the Lord. I think that's a lot to carry for a long time, and now it's lifted. A joyful moment, friends.
